targets.semantic_primary: For an arbitrary graph G, the n-step return probability decays at the spectral radius: rho(G) is the limit of P_o[X_{2n}=o]^{1/2n}, and P_o[X_n=o] <= rho(G)^n for every n.
targets.question_verbatim: Show that for any graph $G$, the spectral radius satisfies $\rho(G)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbf P_o[X_{2n}=o]^{1/2n}$ and $\mathbf P_o[X_n=o]\le\rho(G)^n$ for all $n$.
targets.scope: The two assertions of the exercise only, for any graph G and the simple random walk started at o, with rho(G) the spectral radius of the transition matrix as defined in the chapter body at physical p. 278. The later use of this exercise inside Corollary 7.40 is outside the counted target.

functional_definitions.rho(G): spectral radius of the transition matrix of the simple random walk, defined in the chapter body at physical p. 278
functional_definitions.P_o[X_n=o]: probability that the walk started at o is back at o at time n
